_comment: Crosswalk from the historical layer vocabulary used in
data/gallica_tunisia_maps_features.csv to OpenStreetMap tags, with a
'Rebuild' here does not mean recreating a historical map from OSM - OSM
records the present, so that is impossible. It means: can a modern
counterpart of this layer be assembled from OSM, so the historical sheet
can be compared against it feature by feature.
The confidence values are not guesses about OSM tagging practice in
general. They come from probing OSM inside the published extents of the
data/osm_coverage.json). Counts below are per sheet of roughly 0.06

roads.caveat: The modern network is denser and differently routed. Historical pistes often survive as highway=track, which is the layer to compare against, not the paved network.

railways.observed: up to 59 railway ways per sheet where a line runs
railways.caveat: OSM keeps abandoned and dismantled lines under railway=abandoned/disused, which is what makes the colonial network recoverable at all. Check those tags explicitly or closed lines will be missing.

admin_boundaries.observed: 17 to 26 boundary objects on every sheet probed
admin_boundaries.caveat: Modern governorates and delegations only. Caidats, contrôles civils and the Territoires du Sud have no OSM equivalent - they can be digitised from the historical sheet but not rebuilt from OSM.

settlements.caveat: Node counts look low because a settlement is one node; matching is by name, and Tunisian names in OSM are usually Arabic in `name` with the French form in `name:fr`.

urban_fabric.observed: 1314 to 2019 buildings in settled sheets, 0 in empty ones
urban_fabric.caveat: Present-day fabric. Useful for measuring urban growth against the historical footprint, not for reconstructing the historical medina.

coastline.caveat: Complete and accurate. The one layer where the modern version is strictly better than the historical.

water.caveat: Chotts and sebkhas are mapped inconsistently; oueds are often absent in the interior.

mosques.caveat: Village mosques are reasonably well covered. This is the only religious-building layer with usable OSM coverage.

land_use.caveat: Very uneven. Olive groves are sometimes mapped as landuse=orchard, often not mapped at all.

wells_springs.observed: 0 to 2 typed wells per sheet, against dozens drawn on the 1:50 000 sheets
wells_springs.caveat: Partially recoverable by name instead: 1 to 3 objects per sheet are named Bir or Aïn. Nowhere near the density the historical sheets carry.

shrines_marabouts.observed: zero typed shrines in every sheet probed
shrines_marabouts.caveat: Recoverable only through toponymy: 2 to 3 objects per sheet carry a Sidi, Koubba or Zaouia name. The marabouts drawn on a 1:50 000 sheet cannot be matched to OSM as features.

forts_ksour.observed: zero typed in every sheet probed
forts_ksour.caveat: About one object per sheet is named Ksar or Bordj. The ksour of the south are a conspicuous gap in OSM.

ruins_henchirs.observed: zero typed in every sheet probed
ruins_henchirs.caveat: The henchirs that cover the historical sheets are essentially absent. This layer has to come from the historical maps themselves - which is an argument for digitising them, not a limitation of the corpus.

mines.caveat: The 1930 Gisements miniers map and the geological sheets are the source here, not OSM.

relief.caveat: OSM holds no terrain. Use SRTM or Copernicus DEM instead; contours on the historical sheets can be compared against those.

coastline_bathymetry.caveat: OSM carries no soundings. The hydrographic charts, which are the largest single block of this corpus, have no OSM counterpart for their principal content.

tribes.caveat: Tribal territories are historical and contested; OSM does not carry them.

european_village.caveat: The colonial settler villages exist today as ordinary places, so they are in OSM as settlements - but the distinction the historical map draws between 'Village Français' and the indigenous centre is gone. That distinction is only recoverable from the historical sheet.

telegraph.caveat: The colonial telegraph network is not in OSM in any form.

archaeology.caveat: Major sites such as Carthage, Dougga and El Djem are mapped; the dense scatter of minor sites on the archaeological maps is not.

ports_lighthouses.caveat: Working ports and lighthouses are mapped; historical anchorages and mouillages are not.
